correctness.rationale: For a regular spherical odd-gon, the farthest-vertex cosine-law identity gives sin(rho)=sin(omega/2)/cos(pi/(2n)). All generating vertices lie in the Reuleaux intersection and their vector average proves any containing ball has radius at least rho. The explicit inclusion B_{omega-rho}(o) subset W gives inradius at least omega-rho; Hou--Jin's r+R=omega theorem then gives R<=rho, hence R=rho. Substitution into their definition proves the exact formula and width cancellation. Monotonicity and the expansion are elementary consequences of the closed form.

originality.rationale: The inspected spherical-width papers define the regular Reuleaux construction and establish constant width, while the 2022 Hou--Jin paper introduces the spherical asymmetry and records only the disk/Reuleaux-triangle extremal endpoints in dimension two. The Euclidean regular-Reuleaux formula is explicitly prior-covered by Guo--Jin 2011. Searches found no spherical odd-n formula, no width-independent profile, and no source deriving the spherical circumradius cancellation.

value.rationale: Hou--Jin introduced the invariant specifically for spherical constant-width geometry and singled out the disk and Reuleaux triangle as the two-dimensional extremal endpoints. Regular spherical Reuleaux odd-gons are the canonical finite-arc family between those endpoints. The exact profile shows a non-obvious scale cancellation and exact Euclidean--spherical universality, providing a natural benchmark for further spherical asymmetry calculations rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
